reception: Where the citing literature engages GraphIt, it is mainly as a performance bar. Hardware and accelerator papers measure against its generated code — GraphLily on FPGAs, Capstan for sparsity, work on SpMV-based graph processing — and architecture studies such as Pipette and Dalorex run its programs as workloads, while a GAP-suite evaluation of graph frameworks includes it among those compared. A smaller thread engages the compiler itself, as GraphAttack and Grafs do, and Allo carries the algorithm/schedule separation into accelerator design. Most of the remaining citations are lighter, naming GraphIt among the systems a paper lists or differentiates itself from.
